papers.title: Circadian Oscillation Detection Analysis and Comparison (CODAC):a Multicriteria Method to Estimate and Compare Rhythmicity
papers.summary: CODAC is a multicriteria framework for circadian rhythm detection that integrates nonlinear constrained optimization and avoids single p-value cutoffs. It provides modules for single-group, flexible waveform, pairwise, and multi-group comparisons, showing performance comparable to established methods with added flexibility.

papers.title: Juvenile AAV-Mediated MEF2C Gene Replacement Ameliorates Selected Phenotypes in Mef2c-Haploinsufficient Mice
papers.summary: This study tested juvenile AAV-mediated delivery of MEF2C isoforms in Mef2c-haploinsufficient mice, finding improvements in social novelty, sleep, and selected brain measures, indicating modifiable phenotypes during the juvenile period.

papers.title: MobileSleepNet: A Deployment-Oriented Framework for Sleep Staging on Mobile Devices.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: MobileSleepNet is an ultra-lightweight deep learning framework for sleep staging that runs entirely on mobile devices using single-channel EEG. It achieves accuracy comparable to much larger models on four public datasets and demonstrates low latency and energy consumption in hardware-level profiling and offline mobile evaluation.

papers.title: Exploring the differences in neural oscillation mechanisms before and after sleep deprivation.
papers.summary: Analyzed resting-state EEG from 64 participants under normal sleep and sleep deprivation, finding that theta power variability increased across widespread scalp regions after deprivation and was associated with slower reaction times, suggesting it complements conventional mean spectral measures for characterizing vigilance decline.

papers.title: Acute sleep deprivation alters hypothalamic neuroinflammatory signaling independent of traumatic brain injury in the mouse.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This study examined how acute sleep deprivation affects hypothalamic neuroinflammatory signaling after TBI in mice. Sleep deprivation was the dominant driver of transcriptional changes, particularly in the hypothalamus, with downregulation of MAPK/ERK and inflammatory pathways, and no synergistic effect with TBI.

papers.title: Calibration-free Plug-and-Play EEG-based BCIs.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence
papers.summary: LOTL is an online transfer learning method for EEG-based BCIs that enables calibration-free plug-and-play operation by maintaining global and local hyperplanes for source and target domains. It processes each sample once with a closed-form solution and provides theoretical guarantees, showing effectiveness on four EEG datasets and a real-time BCI system.

papers.title: Keeping in Sync with an Unpredictable Environment: Insights from Circadian Biology.
papers.summary: This review provides a cross-taxonomic synthesis of circadian regulation of output traits, highlighting conserved and taxa-specific mechanisms that rely on synchronization with environmental cycles. It discusses how increasing environmental variability threatens circadian alignment and adaptive relationships across taxa.

papers.title: Circadian rhythms in microglia mediate early life synaptic development in a sex-specific manner.
papers.summary: This study shows that hippocampal microglia in adolescent mice exhibit diurnal transcriptional rhythms of synaptic pruning genes, and that inducible deletion of Bmal1 in microglia abolishes these rhythms, alters developing hippocampal synapses in a sex-specific manner, and leads to impaired memory and sociability.

papers.title: Multimodal circadian phenotyping reveals distinct mechanisms of photic entrainment failure in two sighted patients with non-24-hour sleep-wake disorder.
papers.summary: This case report used multimodal circadian phenotyping in two sighted N24SWD patients, revealing distinct mechanisms of photic entrainment failure: one with preserved melanopsin response but lack of melatonin suppression and a prolonged period, the other with impaired melanopsin response but retained suppression.

papers.title: Wearable Electrodermal Activity Reveals Sustained Sympathetic Responses to Sleep Arousals
papers.summary: This study analyzed synchronized polysomnography and wrist-worn electrodermal activity from 100 adults to characterize sympathetic responses during sleep arousals. They found that arousals elicit sustained EDA modulation persisting up to 40 s post-arousal, primarily driven by clustered sympathetic bursts and amplitude enhancement, providing a quantitative baseline for tracking sympathetic dynamics.

papers.title: Respiratory Effort-Driven Mandibular Opening as a Mechanism of Air Leak During CPAP Therapy.
papers.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
papers.summary: In 200 OSA patients on CPAP, leak periods were associated with increased respiratory effort and mouth opening, with Granger-causality indicating mouth opening preceded by effort and leading to leaks in most cases, suggesting respiratory effort-driven mandibular opening is a key mechanism of unintentional air leak.

papers.title: Differential effects of P2Y12 inhibition on sleep and glymphatic function in male and female mice.
papers.summary: This study pharmacologically inhibited the microglial P2Y12 receptor in male and female mice to assess its role in sleep and glymphatic function. They found sex-differential effects, with females showing greater suppression of glymphatic influx during sleep and more severe sleep fragmentation, suggesting a sex-dependent role for P2Y12 in these processes.

papers.title: Quantitative electroencephalography as a next-generation tool in neurodiagnostics: significance, clinical applications, and practical interpretative frameworks.
papers.summary: This review systematizes knowledge on Quantitative Electroencephalography (QEEG) methodology, clinical applications, and interpretative frameworks. It reports that QEEG can identify electrophysiological subtypes and connectivity dysfunctions in neurodevelopmental, affective, and anxiety disorders, and may help personalize neuromodulatory therapies and monitor pharmacotherapy responses.

papers.title: Delta2Gamma: Band-Wise Adaptive Contrastive Learning of EEG for Alzheimer's Disease Detection
papers.summary: The paper introduces Delta2Gamma, a self-supervised contrastive learning framework for EEG that processes each neural rhythm band with adaptive temperature, achieving 92.4% accuracy in Alzheimer's disease detection from the ADFTD cohort.

papers.title: Moving beyond spike detection: High frequency-driven masking improves seizure onset zone localization in intracranial electroencephalography.
papers.summary: This study benchmarked eight interictal spike detection algorithms on iEEG recordings from 35 epilepsy patients to assess their utility for SOZ localization. They found that IES detection alone has limited spatial specificity, but masking based on spike-HFO co-occurrence markedly improved SOZ localization, achieving a median ratio of 0.89.

papers.title: Predicting big five personality traits from resting-state EEG connectivity: a connectome predictive modeling study.
papers.summary: This study used connectome-based predictive modeling on resting-state EEG connectivity to predict Big Five personality traits in 115 healthy students. Modest cross-validated correlations were found for Conscientiousness (alpha AEC), Extraversion (beta AEC), and Neuroticism (theta dwPLI), with only the Neuroticism model surviving FDR correction.

papers.title: Epileptic arousals: A neglected clinical entity.
papers.summary: This study characterized epileptic arousals (EAs) using simultaneous intracranial and scalp EEG with ECG in 20 focal epilepsy patients. They found that EAs are common (26.2% of seizures), often undetectable by scalp EEG, and exhibit a distinct autonomic signature with greater heart rate modulation compared to physiological arousals, supporting their recognition as a separate seizure type.

papers.title: Circadian skin pH gates IL-33 and remote food sensitization.
papers.summary: In a TEWL-clamped mouse model, circadian skin pH gated IL-33 release and remote food sensitization, with nocturnal injury causing larger systemic IL-33 pulses; acidification suppressed this, and IL-33/ST2 signaling was a necessary checkpoint.

papers.title: Altered early cortical EEG maturation and its relationship to language development in Down syndrome
papers.summary: This study analyzed longitudinal resting-state EEG and developmental data from children with Down syndrome (DS) and typically developing controls, finding altered cortical maturation trajectories in DS, including a decreased aperiodic exponent with age and limited alpha maturation, with a spectral dimension associated with verbal developmental quotient independent of chronological age.

papers.title: Electrophysiological, neurocognitive, and GFAP biomarker responses to corticosteroid therapy in children with ESES/CSWS.
papers.summary: This study evaluated corticosteroid therapy in 11 children with ESES/CSWS, finding that treatment led to seizure reduction, EEG improvement (including complete normalization in 4 patients), and significant decreases in serum GFAP levels, suggesting GFAP as a potential biomarker.

papers.title: A novel algorithm integrating multimodal information for improving OSA-related sleep staging.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a dual-branch multimodal neural network integrating SpO2-derived OSA information to improve sleep staging in OSA patients, achieving competitive performance across three datasets.

papers.title: Insomnia-Associated Circadian and Thrombotic Alterations Coincide with Morning Cardiac Vulnerability.
papers.summary: This study examined the effects of insomnia and myocardial stress on circadian and thrombotic profiles in rats, finding that combined insomnia and stress caused pro-thrombotic cardiac changes predominantly during the light-dark transition, analogous to the human early morning. Integrative transcriptomic analysis identified a circadian-thrombotic molecular signature involving CRY1, F2R, LEP, SSTR2, and IL7R.

papers.title: MDAGCN: A multimodal dynamic adaptive graph convolutional network for sleep staging.
papers.summary: This paper proposes MDAGCN, a multimodal dynamic adaptive graph convolutional network for automated sleep staging using EEG, EOG, EMG, and ECG signals. On ISRUC-S3, it achieves an accuracy of 0.841 and F1-score of 0.825; on Sleep-EDF-78, it achieves the highest accuracy (0.828) and kappa (0.766), demonstrating effectiveness in modeling modality-specific and cross-modal physiological dependencies.

papers.title: Hospital exposome and physiological resilience are associated with postoperative delirium, major complications, and long-term cognitive decline in older adults undergoing cancer surgery: A prospective multidomain cohort study.
The Nutrition-Sleep-Circadian Axis in Age-Related Neurodegeneration: Cellular Mechanisms, Metabolic Dysfunction, and Neuroprotective Interventions.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the interconnected nutrition-sleep-circadian axis in age-related neurodegeneration, focusing on Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. It describes mechanistic crosstalk involving metabolic, mitochondrial, and neuroimmune pathways and evaluates interventions such as chrononutrition and time-restricted feeding as potential therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Respiratory control dysfunction and vulnerability in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from human studies and experimental models demonstrating that respiratory dysfunction in Parkinson's disease (PD) reflects selective vulnerability of brainstem respiratory networks, with alterations in rhythm generation, chemosensitivity, and ventilatory responses. It proposes that respiratory control networks are a mechanistically relevant system in PD, with implications for early diagnosis and targeted therapies.

papers.title: Case Report: non-monotonic longitudinal RSWA with tonic-phasic dissociation across serial attended video-polysomnography in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
Reduced Slow-Wave Sleep and Sleep-Disordered Breathing Are Linked to Suicidal Ideation in Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.summary: This study compared subjective and objective sleep measures in 103 inpatients with major depressive disorder (MDD), with and without suicidal ideation (SI). SI patients had lower N3% sleep and higher apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), and PSQI score, N3%, and AHI independently predicted SI, with a combined model achieving excellent discriminative ability.

papers.title: Alterations in the hepatic drug-metabolizing enzyme network of mice induced by +Gz exposure and its impact on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of modafinil.
papers.summary: This study in mice shows that repeated +Gz exposure reprograms hepatic drug-metabolizing enzymes and functionally inhibits Cyp3a11 activity without altering its expression, leading to delayed absorption and impaired clearance of modafinil.

papers.title: The impact of sleep on resident clinical reasoning: a scoping review.
papers.summary: This scoping review of 31 studies finds that insufficient sleep negatively impacts clinical reasoning learning and performance in medical residents, especially junior residents, highlighting the need for tailored scheduling and learning strategies.

papers.title: Being awake, mood and interest during morning care of adults with moderate to severe intellectual disability using a wake-up light: A practice-based single-case AB design.
Preserved social development but impaired executive function in a Shank3-deficient rat model of Phelan-McDermid syndrome
papers.summary: This study transferred a Shank3 mutation to Long-Evans rats and conducted longitudinal behavioral assessments. Results show preserved social behavior but pronounced executive dysfunction in adults, highlighting cognitive impairment as a key consequence of Shank3 deficiency.

papers.title: "Like Taking Part in Star Wars": Qualitative Study Using Thematic Analysis to Explore the Acceptability and Experiences of Older Adults Participating in Remote Longitudinal Sleep and Dementia Research.
papers.summary: This qualitative study explored the acceptability of remote sleep and dementia research in older adults with and without cognitive impairment, using thematic analysis of interviews and questionnaires. Six themes were identified, with perceived value, trust, simplicity, and support as key facilitators, while burden and usability issues were barriers, suggesting that varying task content and flexibility can improve engagement.

papers.title: Retina-Brain Axis in Postoperative Delirium: Mechanistic Links, Single-Cell/Omics Evidence, and Translational Opportunities.
Sleep disturbances and sleep duration as predictors of working life expectancy among adults aged 50 years and older in Finland.
papers.summary: Using data from two Finnish cohorts, this study estimated working life expectancy from age 50 to 68 by sleep disturbances and duration. Severe sleep disturbances and long sleep duration were associated with approximately 8-9 months shorter working life expectancy compared to no disturbances or mid-range sleep.

papers.title: Effects of dietary nitrate supplementation on peak oxygen uptake following 10 days of Ramadan fasting in healthy adults.
papers.summary: In a randomized trial, 21 healthy adults consumed beetroot juice (nitrate) or control for 10 days during Ramadan fasting. Dietary nitrate supplementation preserved peak oxygen uptake and peak power output, which declined in the control group.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation, Decision Fatigue, and Clinical Performance in Medical Training: A Narrative Review and Perspective on Neurophysiological Monitoring.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on how sleep deprivation and decision fatigue impair clinical performance in medical training, and proposes the CBME-BCI-Fatigue framework to integrate neurophysiological monitoring (EEG, fNIRS) into competency-based assessment. The framework remains conceptual and requires empirical validation.

papers.title: Biopsychosocial profile in individuals with chronic low back pain and high central sensitization symptoms: a cross-sectional comparative study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study compared individuals with chronic low back pain (CLBP) and high vs low central sensitization (CS) symptoms, plus asymptomatic controls. Those with high CS had greater pain intensity, lower pressure pain thresholds, reduced conditioned pain modulation, higher disability, and poorer sleep.

papers.title: Coping strategies mediate the effects of stress on psychological distress in patients with end-stage renal disease: A structural equation modeling approach.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 110 dialysis patients examined relationships among perceived stress, coping strategies, sleep quality, and psychological distress. Coping strategies mediated the effects of stress on sleep disturbance, psychological distress, and quality of life.

papers.title: Real-world effectiveness and safety of lebrikizumab in adults with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis: a retrospective observational study with focus on head and neck involvement.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of 21 adults with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis found that lebrikizumab significantly improved EASI, pruritus, sleep, and DLQI scores, with 77.7% achieving EASI-75 at week 16. Only mild adverse events were reported.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
